newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel markets digest LS deals, cargo swaps up $3.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel markets digest LS deals, cargo swaps up $3.

text.p: European fuel oil markets were turgid on Wednesday, digesting a raft of low sulphur cargo deals from Tuesday and hit by a Dutch holiday, traders said.

With most Dutch traders absent Rotterdam was very quiet, with no fuel barge deals confirmed by mid-afternoon, although one trade at $82 fob ARA was rumoured later. Bid levels were $80 and offer levels $81 fob.
A blitz of low sulphur cargo deals were seen on Tuesday as buyers took advantage of low numbers. One cargo went to Italy and a trader took two more, reportedly for Mediterranean requirements.
A British utility buyer was also rumoured to have bought, but this could not be confirmed.
Traders said physical values were still around $85/$86 with most doubting it would climb in the thin business expected in the remainder of the holiday-hit week.
Paper cargo markets were strong, but thinly traded,
recovering to hit $87/$88 on the back of stronger crude, the
clear-out of prompt cargoes and a desire to maintain the
differential with high sulphur swaps, traders said.
